query:
is my abstract too long for Nature? it's 260 words:

Turbulent channel flows over riblets are a classic test case for passive drag reduction. Riblets aligned with the flow reduce skin friction by up to 8% in laboratory experiments, but how this reduction scales with Reynolds number remains debated, because most data come from friction Reynolds numbers below 1000. In this paper we present direct numerical simulations of channel flow over trapezoidal riblets at friction Reynolds numbers of 180, 550 and 1000, on grids of up to 2.1 billion points. Simulations were run on 4096 GPUs for a total of 3.2 million GPU hours. We find that drag reduction decreases from 7.2% to 5.1% across this range, and that the decrease follows the log-law shift predicted by García-Mayoral and Jiménez. These results suggest that riblets remain useful at flight Reynolds numbers, but with smaller benefits than laboratory data imply.
